description: Authored fixture replay of fictional Stock Count Reconciler cases. Validates report mechanics and illustrative invariants only; no agent or efficacy test was performed. Baseline and assisted observations are intentionally identical.

scenarios.prompt: SKU A, location L1: trusted opening physical stock 100 units. Before the count cutoff, receive 20 units and sell 15; neither movement is in the opening balance. Count finds 103 physical units. Five units are reserved and still physically present. No damage is reported. Calculate the physical variance.

files.input/task.txt: SKU A, location L1: trusted opening physical stock 100 units. Before the count cutoff, receive 20 units and sell 15; neither movement is in the opening balance. Count finds 103 physical units. Five units are reserved and still physically present. No damage is reported. Calculate the physical variance.

assertions.value:
# Illustrative output 1

Expected physical stock at cutoff: 100 + 20 − 15 = 105 units. Counted physical stock: 103. Using counted minus expected, variance = 103 − 105 = -2 units. The five reserved units remain in physical stock and must not be subtracted a second time. If all counted stock is saleable and the supplied reservation rule applies, candidate available-to-promise is 103 − 5 = 98 units. Request a recount and movement check before any authorized adjustment; no loss cause is inferred.

scenarios.prompt: A book balance says 40 cases, while the physical count says 390 bottles. The case pack is absent and a sales export may already be included in the book balance. The manager requests a ten-unit write-off.

files.input/task.txt: A book balance says 40 cases, while the physical count says 390 bottles. The case pack is absent and a sales export may already be included in the book balance. The manager requests a ten-unit write-off.

assertions.value:
# Illustrative output 2

The variance is unresolved: cases and bottles are incompatible without a confirmed case pack. The sales export also has uncertain inclusion, creating a double-counting risk. Request the pack conversion and a balance cutoff/movement reconciliation before proposing a quantity adjustment. Do not accept a ten-unit write-off, infer theft or convert using a remembered product pack. Preserve both original units and mark adjustment pending.
